source: Comics idiom reference — drawing, colour and panel grammar
_note: Each entry is a drawing system, not a named artist's likeness of a work. Where a movement or house style is named it is named as attribution for a technique, the same way the cinematography shelf credits a director of photography.

entries.name: Golden Age Newsprint
entries.summary: Four-colour process on absorbent newsprint. The registration errors are the look.
entries.detail: Flat CMY at 25/50/100% with a heavy black plate, printed on paper that spreads the ink. Registration drifts by a hair, so colours peek out past their linework — reproducing that misregistration is what separates the period look from a modern flat-colour pastiche.

prompt: four-colour newsprint process, benday dot screens visible
heavy uniform black ink line, no line weight modulation
flat colour at 25/50/100 percent tints only
slight plate misregistration, colour offset past the linework
warm yellowed paper stock, ink spread and bleed

entries.why: The registration errors are the look — period colour as a printing accident, not a filter.
entries.how: Four-colour process on absorbent newsprint, CMY at 25/50/100% with a heavy black plate.

entries.name: EC Horror
entries.summary: Meticulous crosshatched rendering doing genuinely nasty things, at newsstand size.
entries.detail: The tension is between craftsmanship and content: the linework is patient, academic and beautifully controlled, and it is being spent on a rotting corpse. Dense feathered crosshatch for form, heavy spot blacks for mood, and a caption box that will not stop talking.

prompt: dense feathered crosshatch rendering for tonal form
heavy spot blacks and dramatic cast shadow
lurid four-colour palette on newsprint
high-contrast horror lighting from below
ornate caption boxes and hand lettering

entries.name: Kinetic Superhero
entries.summary: Anatomy sacrificed to force. Everything is mid-explosion and coming at you.
entries.detail: Extreme foreshortening on a wide-angle virtual lens, figures bursting the panel border, and abstract energy crackle standing in for physics. Blocky, slab-like anatomy — musculature drawn as engineering rather than biology.

prompt: extreme foreshortening, fist or foot thrust at the viewer
blocky slab-built anatomy, exaggerated musculature
figures breaking the panel border
abstract black energy crackle and photo-collage texture
bold four-colour flats, heavy black holding line

entries.name: Ligne Claire
entries.summary: One uniform line, flat colour, no shadow. Everything equally in focus.
entries.detail: The Franco-Belgian discipline: a single unvarying line weight for every object at every distance, flat unmodulated colour, and no hatching or cast shadow anywhere. Depth comes entirely from overlap and from colour temperature, which forces the drawing to be structurally correct.

prompt: uniform unvarying line weight throughout, no tapering
flat unmodulated colour fills, no gradients
no hatching, no cast shadows, no rendering
depth by overlap and colour temperature only
architecturally precise backgrounds, everything equally sharp

entries.name: Fine-Line Science Fantasy
entries.summary: Hairline pen, enormous vistas, and a palette that has no business being that calm.
entries.detail: A very fine, even technical-pen line describing extraordinary density of detail without ever getting heavy, over flat washes in unexpected desert pastels. Figures are small; the world is the subject.

prompt: hairline technical pen work, even weight, extraordinary detail density
vast landscape with a small figure for scale
flat pastel washes — sand, rose, pale turquoise
organic biomechanical architecture
no black spotting, tone built entirely from line density

entries.name: Ink Chiaroscuro Noir
entries.summary: Pure black and pure white, no grey. The reader assembles the image.
entries.detail: Every tone is a decision to leave paper or fill it — there is no rendering in between. Rain becomes white scratches on black; a face becomes two shapes and an eye. Works because the eye completes what the ink refuses to state.

prompt: pure black and white only, no greys, no halftone
figures reduced to silhouette and negative-space shapes
white rain scratched into solid black fields
extreme high-contrast expressionist lighting
occasional single spot colour on one element

entries.name: The Nine-Panel Grid
entries.summary: A rigid 3×3 that never varies, so every break from it detonates.
entries.detail: A structural choice more than a drawing style: identical panel size throughout, which forces the storytelling to work through composition and rhyme instead of layout drama. Because the grid is absolute, a single splash page carries the weight a whole sequence would elsewhere.

prompt: strict three by three panel grid, identical panel dimensions
even naturalistic rendering, deliberately undramatic
muted period colour, purple and orange complementary scheme
composition rhymes between corresponding panels
dense caption text overlaying the image

entries.name: Shōnen Manga
entries.summary: Screentone, speed lines, and a page built to be read in eleven seconds.
entries.detail: Monochrome with adhesive screentone doing all the tonal work. Layouts break the rectangle constantly — diagonal gutters, figures crossing panels — and impact frames go full bleed. Read right to left, which changes where the eye lands.

prompt: monochrome ink with adhesive screentone dot shading
radiating speed lines and impact focus lines
diagonal irregular panel gutters, figures crossing borders
exaggerated expression, sweat drops and emotive symbols
right-to-left reading order

entries.name: Gekiga
entries.summary: Manga's adult register: heavier line, slower pacing, nothing cute.
entries.detail: Coined to distance itself from 'manga' as children's work. Realistic proportions, weathered faces, dense environmental detail, and long wordless sequences of nothing much happening — the pacing is the argument.

prompt: heavy brush-inked line with realistic proportion
dense hatched environmental detail, urban decay
long wordless panel sequences, ordinary action
coarse screentone, high tonal contrast
weathered specific faces, no stylised cuteness

entries.name: Shōjo Manga
entries.summary: Panels dissolve, flowers erupt, and interior feeling overrides physical space.
entries.detail: The most formally radical mainstream comics grammar: panel borders vanish, backgrounds become symbolic pattern, and a character's emotional state literally replaces the room they are standing in. Delicate line, enormous eyes, screentone used decoratively rather than tonally.

prompt: borderless dissolving panels bleeding into each other
symbolic decorative backgrounds — flowers, sparkles, screentone pattern
very large detailed eyes with multiple highlights
delicate fine variable line weight
figure floating free of any physical setting

entries.name: Vertical Scroll Webtoon
entries.summary: One continuous column. Pacing is measured in scroll distance, not page turns.
entries.detail: Built for a thumb: a single infinite vertical strip, full digital colour, generous empty space between beats because whitespace is the only pacing tool left when there is no page turn. Compositions are tall and centred, never wide.

prompt: single continuous vertical composition, tall narrow framing
full digital colour with soft airbrushed shading
generous empty vertical space between story beats
clean digital line, uniform weight
centred subject, no wide horizontal compositions

entries.name: Underground Comix
entries.summary: Obsessive crosshatch, bad vibes, and no editor whatsoever.
entries.detail: Dense nervous crosshatching over grotesque caricature, hand-lettered wall to wall, printed cheap on bad paper. The visual density is anxiety made legible.

prompt: obsessive nervous crosshatch covering every surface
grotesque exaggerated caricature, bulbous distorted anatomy
hand lettering crammed into every available space
cheap offset print on coarse paper, muddy registration
claustrophobic composition with no empty space

entries.name: Architectural Shadow
entries.summary: Design by subtraction — huge black shapes with a few decisive lines left over.
entries.detail: Figures and environments built as flat interlocking black shapes rather than drawn and then shaded. Detail appears only where it is load-bearing; everywhere else is solid ink. Colour is applied in flat unmodulated fields, usually one dominant hue per scene.

prompt: massive flat interlocking black shapes defining form
minimal decisive linework only where structurally necessary
flat unmodulated colour fields, one dominant hue per scene
folk-art and woodcut influenced silhouette design
geometric rubble, ornament and architectural pattern

entries.name: Bande Dessinée Album
entries.summary: Large-format, painted, and unhurried. A page is composed as a page.
entries.detail: The European album tradition: A4 hardcover, forty-eight pages, full painted or richly rendered colour, and layouts composed for the whole spread rather than assembled panel by panel. Backgrounds are researched.

prompt: richly painted colour with visible brush and watercolour texture
researched architecturally accurate backgrounds
regular tier-based page layout composed as a whole spread
naturalistic proportion, restrained expression
large format detail density

entries.name: Silver Age Four-Colour
entries.summary: Optimistic primaries, confident line, benday dots you can count.
entries.detail: Cleaner and brighter than the Golden Age — better paper, better registration, and a house line style that is confident rather than crude. Benday dots are large enough to read as texture at arm's length, which is the signature.

prompt: large visible benday dot screens, countable at reading distance
confident even-weight ink outline
bright optimistic primary palette, red yellow blue dominant
clean registration on improved paper stock
heroic upright posing, clear silhouette

entries.name: Autobiographical Indie
entries.summary: Small, plain, honest. Deliberately unimpressive drawing doing precise work.
entries.detail: A drawing style that refuses virtuosity so the reader trusts it: simple confident line, minimal or no shading, rigid small-panel grid, and figures that stay consistent rather than beautiful. Usually monochrome or a single flat spot colour.

prompt: simple confident unshowy line, minimal shading
small regular panel grid, many panels per page
monochrome or a single flat muted spot colour
consistent simplified figures, mundane domestic settings
hand lettering in the artist's own hand

entries.name: Risograph Zine
entries.summary: Two spot inks, misregistered on purpose, and the overprint is the third colour.
entries.detail: Soy-ink duplication in a small number of fluorescent spot colours. Each colour is a separate pass, so registration drifts, and where two passes overlap you get a colour neither ink can make alone. Grain, streaking and roller marks are features.

prompt: two or three fluorescent spot inks, layered separations
deliberate misregistration between colour passes
overprint multiply where colours cross
visible paper grain, roller streaking, ink mottling
coarse halftone screens at a visible angle

entries.name: Fully Painted Graphic Novel
entries.summary: No holding line at all. Form is described entirely by paint.
entries.detail: Oil or acrylic rendered directly, with the ink outline abandoned — which removes the single most comic-like element and pushes the page toward illustration. Panels usually float on a plain field with no border.

prompt: fully painted rendering with no ink holding line
form described by value and edge quality alone
oil or acrylic texture, visible brushwork
borderless panels floating on a plain field
naturalistic light with real falloff and bounce
